topic: Continence assessment and care in older inpatients

audits.title: 297 Assessing continence care in a rehabilitation unit: insights from an audit
audits.standard: Royal College of Physicians National Audit of Continence Care (NACC) standard
audits.setting: Medical gerontology rehabilitation ward, Tallaght University Hospital

cycle1.result: 26 (83.9%) wore incontinence wear, 21 (80.8%) by choice; urinary incontinence documented in 13 (41.9%).

audits.intervention: Continence added to NCHD teaching schedule and MDT proforma adjusted to include a patient-specific continence record.

cycle2.result: 27 (67.5%) wore incontinence wear, 19 (70%) by choice; urinary incontinence documented in 18 (45.7%).

audits.other_findings: Prevalence of incontinence unchanged; many patients preferred incontinence wear, so future work should engage patients.
audits.citation: Davey N, Merron G, El Eraky N, Pereppadan B, Fallon A, McDonough A. 297 Assessing continence care in a rehabilitation unit: insights from an audit. Age and Ageing. 2023;52(Supplement_3). doi:10.1093/ageing/afad156.235.

audits.title: Assessment Of Hospital-acquired Incontinence In An Acute Hospital: A Re-audit
audits.standard: Royal College of Physicians National Audit of Continence Care (NACC) standard
audits.setting: General medical and surgical wards, Tallaght University Hospital, Dublin, patients over 65

cycle1.period: Three-day period at start of continence awareness month
cycle1.result: All had documented continence status; of 44 continent pre-admission, 12 had incontinence wear as inpatients.

cycle2.result: All had documented continence status; of 40 continent pre-admission, 14 had incontinence wear as inpatients.

audits.other_findings: Rationale for incontinence wear varied and was sometimes undocumented; use increased between audits.
audits.citation: Singh M, Buckley E, Dunne P, Maguire P, Doyle P, Coughlan T. Assessment Of Hospital-acquired Incontinence In An Acute Hospital: A Re-audit. Age and Ageing. 2025;54(Supplement_4). doi:10.1093/ageing/afaf318.134.

audits.title: Fit For Purpose: A Continence Wear Clinical Audit
audits.standard: HSE Guideline for the assessment, promotion and management of continence in adults by registered nurses (2020)
audits.setting: St Vincent's University Hospital, Dublin, model 4 teaching hospital medical wards

cycle1.result: 12/76 (15.8%) incontinent before admission but 41 (54%) wearing continence wear at audit; of 64 not incontinent at admission, 22 (34.4%) felt they needed continence products.

audits.other_findings: Over 50% of patients were unaware of more appropriate continence products; staff education and review of continence assessment documentation recommended.
audits.citation: Collopy A, Broderick C, Boyle N. Fit For Purpose: A Continence Wear Clinical Audit. Age and Ageing. 2025;54(Supplement_4). doi:10.1093/ageing/afaf318.171.

audits.title: 147 Assessing Assessment: An Audit of Continence Assessment and Documentation in a City Centre Teaching Hospital
audits.standard: Audit tool adapted from the RCP National Continence Audit tool and the hospital elimination documentation pathway
audits.setting: General medical ward and specialist geriatric medicine ward, city centre teaching hospital (Mercy University Hospital, Cork)

cycle1.result: 4 patients had no continence status documented; of over-65s with documented incontinence (42%), only 40% had the nursing elimination section fully completed; 6 had symptoms/type documented; catheter indications documented in both catheterised patients.

audits.other_findings: An assessment tool and education programme were planned for the geriatric ward.
audits.citation: Randles M, Hayes M, Cotter S, Saramago I, McGrath K, O'Caoimh R, et al.. 147 Assessing Assessment: An Audit of Continence Assessment and Documentation in a City Centre Teaching Hospital. Age and Ageing. 2019;48(Supplement_3):iii17-iii65. doi:10.1093/ageing/afz103.88.

audits.title: National audit of continence care for older people: results of a pilot study*.
audits.standard: Good Practice in Continence Services and the National Service Framework milestone for integrated continence services
audits.setting: 15 randomly selected primary care, secondary care and care home sites (national pilot)

cycle1.result: 85% of hospitals had no written continence policy; access to integrated continence services was inadequate; deficiencies in assessment, examination and investigation.

audits.other_findings: The audit tool was reliable (median kappa 0.7); catheter use was high in secondary care.
audits.citation: Wagg A, Mian S, Lowe D, Potter J, Pearson M, Continence Programme Working Party. National audit of continence care for older people: results of a pilot study*. J Eval Clin Pract. 2005;11(6):525-532. doi:10.1111/j.1365-2753.2005.00570.x. PMID: 16364105.

audits.title: National audit of continence care for older people: management of urinary incontinence.
audits.standard: National Service Framework for Older People: integrated continence services by April 2004; DH Good practice in continence services
audits.setting: National audit: primary care trusts, secondary care trusts (198 hospitals) and care homes in England, Wales and Northern Ireland

cycle1.result: Returns from 141/326 (43%) PCTs, 159/196 (81%) secondary care trusts and 29/309 (9%) care homes; integrated services reported by 58% of PCTs, 48% of hospitals and 74% of care homes.

audits.other_findings: Deficiencies in assessment and management of urinary incontinence; basic care by direct carers often lacking.
audits.citation: Wagg A, Potter J, Peel P, Irwin P, Lowe D, Pearson M. National audit of continence care for older people: management of urinary incontinence. Age Ageing. 2008;37(1):39-44. doi:10.1093/ageing/afm163. PMID: 18033776.

audits.title: Closing the loop in an audit of urinary incontinence.
audits.standard: Minimum standards for history taking, physical examination and investigation of urinary incontinence
audits.setting: Assessment and Rehabilitation and Continuing Care wards, Department of Medicine for the Elderly, Royal Victoria Hospital, Dundee

cycle1.result: Assessment and Rehabilitation wards: history 60%, examination 50%, investigation 100%.

audits.intervention: Full discussion of results with staff.

cycle2.result: Assessment and Rehabilitation wards: history 57%, examination 24%, investigation 86%; Continuing Care wards: history 17%, examination 14%, investigation 47%.

audits.other_findings: 40% of 368 patients had urinary incontinence; care plans improved to 71% (Assessment and Rehabilitation) and 97% (Continuing Care).
audits.citation: Stewart CI, McMurdo ME. Closing the loop in an audit of urinary incontinence. Scott Med J. 1995;40(1):21-22. doi:10.1177/003693309504000109. PMID: 7604238.
